page: OVHcloud b3-16 is a general-purpose cloud server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The CPU configuration includes a 32 MB L3 cache and supports hardware-assisted virtualization via AMD SVM, alongside instruction sets such as AVX, AES, and SHA_NI. The server is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core.

The instance is deployed on a KVM hypervisor and includes 100 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and the server is allocated one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing and Geekbench text processing scoring in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and cryptographic operations fall within the average range. However, the server exhibits lower throughput in specific workloads, with static web serving and prompt processing for medium-sized (7B) language models scoring in the bottom 25%.

With its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-core ratio, the b3-16 offers a predictable resource profile for general-purpose workloads. It is well-suited for applications requiring consistent single-core performance, such as text processing, lightweight database operations, and general application hosting, though it may be less efficient for high-throughput web serving or intensive multi-threaded tasks.
